perspective:
**Christian Mensah’s available information:**

- He is a Black male police officer and has a close childhood friendship with Jonathan Balogun. Christian often seeks Jonathan’s advice and values his more educated perspective.
- Christian had been feeling that Jonathan was hiding something important, which made him anxious and suspicious. He arranged a meeting with Jonathan at their favorite coffee shop.
- Christian told Jonathan he felt Jonathan was hiding something. He heard Jonathan admit that he had been keeping something from him and was in trouble, but had not known how to tell him.
- Christian felt worried and empathetic. He told Jonathan he wanted to help and that they could face it together. Jonathan replied that the situation was complicated and he did not want to drag Christian into it. Christian insisted he was Jonathan’s best friend and would do everything he could. Jonathan said he could use support and resources and needed a way out of the mess.
- Christian began to believe Jonathan’s trouble might be related to criminal activity. He asked Jonathan if it was illegal. Jonathan said he could not say for sure, that he might have gotten involved with the wrong people, but that he had not done anything illegal himself. Christian said he understood, wanted Jonathan safe, and would look into it discreetly. Jonathan thanked him and trusted him to handle it carefully.
- Christian’s investigation led him to believe Jonathan was being framed by someone trying to set him up. He told Jonathan this, said he had leads but not certainty, and planned to gather more evidence to prove Jonathan’s innocence. Jonathan thanked him.
- Christian came to believe the real culprit was someone close to both him and Jonathan. He told Jonathan he had found out who was behind it—someone they both knew and trusted—and planned to confront them and bring them to justice. Jonathan warned him that the person was dangerous but trusted Christian to do what was right.
